newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-SMALL CLUBS FROZEN OUT IN F.A. CUP ADVENTURE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SMALL CLUBS FROZEN OUT IN F.A. CUP ADVENTURE.

text.p: The big freeze gripping Europe has done its best to delay the giant-killing aspirations of England's smaller clubs in this weekend's F.A. Cup third round.
Frost and snow had forced the postponement of 10 of the 32 games by 1315 GMT on Friday, including the match at minor league Hednesford. Two more venues faced pitch inspections later in the day.
As a result, interest centred on England's big guns -- the premier league clubs with realistic F.A. Cup hopes and, more importantly on one of the coldest New Years of the century, under-soil heating.

The tie of the round is undoubtedly Sunday's match at Old Trafford between holders Manchester United and Tottenham -- the competition's two most successful sides -- but Saturday's fixtures also throw up a few major clashes.
Tottenham's north London neighbours Arsenal face fellow premier league side and 1973 Cup winners Sunderland at Highbury, scene of a stormy league encounter between them in September.

Arsenal won that match 2-0 after Paul Stewart and Martin Scott had been sent off for the visitors and Sunderland boss Peter Reid, an F.A. Cup winner with Everton in 1984, had been banished to the stands for dissent.
Arsene Wenger's side, six times F.A. Cup winners and six times beaten finalists, will be looking for a repeat of the last time the two sides met in the third round in January 1991.
The Gunners won that tie 2-1 to start a run which took them to the semifinals, where they were finally beaten by arch-rivals Tottenham.
Premier league strugglers Nottingham Forest take on Ipswich at home in a tie which smacks of the late 1970s.
Ipswich won the F.A. Cup for the first and only time in 1978, the year Forest gained their solitary English league title.

The two sides dominated English and continental football for the next three years. Forest won the European Cup twice in succession while Ipswich lifted the UEFA Cup and twice finished as runners-up in the league.
Since then the stars of both clubs have waned -- Ipswich are in the first division and Forest could join them if they do not get their act together.
Another former glory team are Burnley, one of English football's old-time northern powerhouses, F.A. Cup winners in 1914 and beaten finalists in 1947 and 1962.
They travel to Anfield to meet last year's runners-up Liverpool, top of the league and 5-1 favourites to lift the cup for the sixth time.
Burnley beat the Reds in the semifinal on their way to lifting the first F.A. Cup to be staged after World War Two, but since then Liverpool have been in the ascendency.
On the last four occasions the two sides have met in the cup -- in 1963, 1969, 1973 and 1979 -- the Merseysiders have won.
A combination of frost and first and second round results has limited the scope for giant-killing this weekend.
With Hednesford's tie against second division York postponed, Woking and Stevenage are the only minor league representatives in action.
Woking travel to 1987 winners Coventry, unbeaten in their last five premier league outings and in no mood for an early exit, while Stevenage appear up the road at first division Birmingham.
